The appellants are the unsuccessful Opposite parties
in CD 30/2004 before the District
Forum, Ranga Reddy where under an order was passed
directing them to return a sum of Rs.1,36,532/- with interest at 9% 5.7.2001
till realization with costs . Aggrieved by the impugned order this appeal is
filed questioning the legality and
propriety of it.
The facts of the case in brief are that on oral negotiations the opposite party company agreed to supply
electronic weighing machine. The complainant had sent a quotation requesting OP
1 for supply of electronic belt weighers which was accepted on 19.8.99. Subsequently the OPs through letter dated 4.9.21999 had given the offer for
supplying the equipment for Rs.1,65,000/-
for taxes etc. A purchase order was issued in favour of OP 1 for
the said equipment. As per the purchase order, delivery is to be made within
three months so also that integrator
Master weigher-1 with accuracy 0.05 % ( + or - ). Though important
conditions were mentioned while supplying equipment, but the equipment
was supplied on 13.4.2000 and their Service Engineer was deputed in My 2000 only after repeated reminders. It
was found that the machine was not supplied as per the specifications and terms
and conditions of the purchase order. During the trial run it had recorded
abnormal variations upto 4 to 10% which was informed to the respondents
and a meeting was conducted on 14.7.2001. Minutes were recorded. It was
confirmed that the equipment needs calibration and it will be done only by a
senior engineer. Fax message was sent to respondents to depute senior engineer
on 29.8.2001. One Krishna Kishore was sent to
undertake repairs who informed that the master weigh needs repairs which can be
done at their plant. It was confirmed by the letter dated 31.8.2001 and
undertaking by the respondent get it repaired. Later it Master weigher 5 was
replaced. On trial run in the presence of Service Engineer even master weigher- 5 also shows verification more than from 4 to
10% and it was duly intimated. But the
respondents have least bothered in getting the equipment successfully commissioned. On 30.8.2002 one Mohd. Khasim was deputed by the
respondent for commissioning of the belt
weigher who confirmed that load cell is not functioning which requires replacement. Minutes were
recorded. Respondents neglected
thereafter. So the complaint was filed
for successful commissioning of
the equipment or for refund of the amount. The act or omission
amounts to deficiency . Hence filed the complaint for directing to rectify the
equipment for refund of Rs.1,65,000 with compensation.
The Opposite parties
have engaged an advocate who filed vakalat on 5.5.2004 but he had not filed any
counter. So the District forum had
forfeited the right of the appellants/OPs in filing
the counter.
Basing on the evidence and Ex.A1 to A11 filed by the
complainant and hearing the OPs counsel the District forum passed the order
directing the Opposite parties to pay
Rs.1,36,532/- with interest at 9% pa from 5.7.2001 till final realization with
costs.
The appellants in their grounds of appeal, have taken
the stand that the District Forum had erred in not considering the fact that the
mother board supplied by the appellants was damaged due to high voltage at the
site and also failed to consider
that the weigher
which was commissioned by them was
handed over in perfect and good
working condition since July, 2001 to 30th August, 2002. It is further contended that the District
Forum has failed to consider the fact that the load cell which was damaged was
not due to the fault of the appellant but due to the overloading or defect in
the conveyor structure of the respondent .It has also raised the contention
that the warranty period expired long back which fact was not considered and
more particularly that the transaction was for commercial purpose as such
complainant is not consumer as per the provisions of the C. P. Act.
It can be said
without any hesitation that the appellants/OPs
held no opportunity to put forth their
case before the District Forum and their right to file their version was
forfeited as they have not filed their
version or counter within 45 days. No
doubt, Ex. A2 to A11 confirms that the complainant had placed an order with OP
for supplying of weighing machine as per their requirement and the same was
installed and commissioned. But at the
outset it can be said that the respondents/ complainants have not filed the
warranty given by the manufacturer from the date of purchase or the date of
delivery. Apart from it, there is no evidence on record to show that the
weighing machine that was supplied is
having any manufacturing defect or failed to have its utility as per its specifications. There is no expert technical
opinion about he dysfunction or defect
in equipment in question. Maintainability
of the complaint is a question of
law which can be seen at any stage of the case while considering the merits and
demerits of the case.
It is an undisputed fact that the complainant is a
company registered under companies Act and that this complaint was filed on
28.11.2003 by means of amendment of the
definition of consumer by an Act 62/2002 the commercial transactions are
curtailed from the definition of consumer so also any claim filed by the
companies who are dealing with commercial transactions. The amendment has come into effect from
23.3.2003 while so this complaint was filed subsequent to the amendment of the
section.
The appellants/opposite parties cannot plead that the
machinery was purchased for commercial purposes. Even though a company or firm having
business for commercial purposes is not a consumer, but in respect of goods
sold and supplied which are defective or dysfunctions, the purchaser may file a
claim for replacement of machinery or refund
of the amount paid. But the said
claim is to be filed within warranty
period. If the claim is filed after the expiry of warranty period, it is for
the complainant/purchaser to prove that the goods supplied are totally
defective which is to be established by producing technical experts evidence
and the same is not at all filed.
Through Ex.A-10 dated 16.12.2002, appellants/opposite parties
informed the complainant that the
warranty had expired 30 months back from the date of purchase. The purchase order was on 25.09.99 ( Ex.
A5) and the date of erection was on 31.01.2001, while so the
complaint was filed on 28.11.2003. The
exchange of letters will not extend the limitation at all. Thus it is clear hat
the complaint was filed beyond a period of two years and thereby it is barred by limitation U/s.24-
A of the
Consumer Protection Act
. No condonation was sought at
all.
In the result, the appeal is allowed setting aide the
order of the District Forum. Consequently the complaint is dismissed. No order
as costs.
